author: Ramon Antonio Vargas and agencies
description:
Prosecutors allege Moises Freire gave two students at FIT the opioid, saying it was cocaine, and raped one as she overdosed

A man raped a student at New York’s Fashion Institute of Technology (FIT) after giving her a dose of fentanyl that rendered her unconscious and ultimately killed her, federal prosecutors allege.

That student’s friend also experienced an overdose and nearly died after taking the potent synthetic opiate, leading to charges against three men, the US justice department said in a statement on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: New York man charged with rape and lethal fentanyl dosing of college student

author: Associated Press and Agence France-Presse
description:
Disgraced music mogul moved to Pennsylvania prison after reports of perks and fight injuries at New Jersey lockup

Sean “Diddy” Combs, who was convicted of prostitution-related crimes, has been moved to a federal prison in Pennsylvania after reports that the disgraced music producer was living the high life and was injured in a fight at his New Jersey lockup, according to reports.

The US Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is transferring Combs, 56, from FCI Fort Dix to FCI Allenwood Low, a low-security facility south of Williamsport and about 155 miles (250km) west of New York City, a person familiar with the matter said to the Associated Press. The person was not authorized to speak publicly and did so on condition of anonymity.
title: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs moved to new prison after reports of a luxury lifestyle behind bars

author: Gabrielle Canon
description:
Kaylub Giamanco, who was reportedly driving home when he heard gunshots, ‘not seeking recognition’, family says

Details are beginning to emerge about Kaylub Giamanco, the man who brought the deadly shooting at elementary school in Bend, Oregon on Thursday, to an end by fatally shooting the 16-year-old suspect in the midst of a violent rampage.

Authorities have yet to officially release the man’s identity, but Kaylub Giamanco’s family issued a statement on Friday confirming that he shot and killed the suspect.

Continue reading...
title: Bystander who killed Oregon shooter identified as father of girls at elementary school

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem died after reportedly ‘passing out’ and falling off Goliath rollercoaster in Georgia

The family of a man who was ejected from a rollercoaster at a Six Flags amusement park in Georgia and died has publicly questioned whether the death could have been prevented.

Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was riding the Goliath rollercoaster at Six Flags Over Georgia near Atlanta alongside his niece during a family trip to celebrate her birthday when he was thrown from the ride. His niece witnessed her uncle’s death, a relative told the Atlanta ABC News affiliate WSB-TV.
title: Family of US man who died on Six Flags ride question if death was preventable

author: Jonathan Watts
description:
Forest clearance at smallest total since records began in 1988 in success for Lula ahead of presidential run-off

Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon has fallen to its lowest level since records began, new government data shows.

But whether this globally important success is maintained or reversed is on a knife edge ahead of a presidential election run-off on 25 October between two candidates with sharply different visions for the future of the rainforest and how that affects relations with the US under Donald Trump.

Continue reading...
title: Brazilian Amazon deforestation falls to lowest on record as pivotal vote looms

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Lawyers tell high court that client could harm himself if serious allegations against him are made public

A “well-known individual” is trying to secure a permanent injunction against the Guardian and ITN to prevent them from publishing details of serious allegations made against him.

At a high court hearing on Friday, the claimant’s legal team said there was a serious risk that he could harm himself should the allegations be made public.

In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline on 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text HOME to 741741 to connect with a crisis counselor. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other internation
title: ‘Well-known individual’ tries to secure permanent injunction against Guardian and ITN

author: Rowena Mason, Lisa O’Carroll and Jasper Jolly
description:
Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe package

No 10 has left the door open to imposing tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles as part of the Made in Europe package, prompting a warning from Beijing that such a move would be “discriminatory”.

Downing Street said on Friday that it would “welcome the objective to have the UK included in the Industrial Accelerator Act” after France dropped its opposition to Britain joining the scheme.

Continue reading...
title: No 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU scheme

author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels and Andrew Rothin Kyiv
description:
Ukrainian president says US limiting access was a ‘dangerous and unpleasant surprise’, amid reports the order came from inside White House

  • Europe live – latest updates

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said the Ukrainian military’s access to the Starlink satellite internet service has not yet been fully restored, as media reports suggested the order to throttle the service had come from within the White House.

Zelenskyy met European leaders on Friday in Brussels, where he asked the EU for another €70bn (£60bn) next year to fund Ukraine’s defence against Russia.

Continue reading...
title: Starlink access still not fully restored for Ukraine’s military, says Zelenskyy

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Inquiry said to have been launched after force received report ‘relating to alleged unauthorised access of a political party’s database’

Police are carrying out a criminal investigation into a row over the founding of Your Party, which split the leftwing party as it was established last year.

A spokesperson for London’s Metropolitan police said they had launched an investigation after they received a report in September 2025 “relating to the alleged unauthorised access of a political party’s database”, the Politico website reported.

Continue reading...
title: Met police investigating row over founding of Your Party

author: Robyn Vinter and Rachel Hall
description:
Author Sarah Helm, married to Jonathan Powell, wrote to back novelist Sally Rooney’s support of proscribed direct action group

The UK’s national security adviser, Jonathan Powell, is under pressure to distance himself from a comment made by his wife, the award-winning writer Sarah Helm, in support of Palestine Action.

The post was made in defence of the critically acclaimed Irish novelist Sally Rooney, who said she had been forced to pull her books from shelves in the UK after pledging proceeds from their sales to Palestine Action.

Continue reading...
title: UK national security adviser under pressure over wife’s comment on supporting Palestine Action

author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
description:
Lula reverses position on age of responsibility for ‘heinous’ crimes in what many see as a desperate electoral gambit

Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has announced that he now supports lowering the age of criminal responsibility for “heinous” crimes from 18 to 16, reversing a longstanding policy in what is widely seen as a desperate electoral gambit.

The U-turn, which Lula announced during a Thursday night interview with TV Globo, comes with the presidential runoff in just over a week. The incumbent faces an uphill battle to overturn the first-round victory of his opponent, the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who remains slightly ahead at the polls.

Continue reading...
title: Brazil’s Lula says he now backs lowering age of criminal responsibility to 16

author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
description:
Speaking at live UK event, former US president expresses hope rooted in the past and discusses the modern challenges to democracy

Barack Obama cited the “wonderful” story of how Manchester cotton workers stood in solidarity with enslaved African Americans as an inspiration for our times in a live appearance in the city.

Tens of thousands of people packed Co-op Live in the city on Thursday for An Evening With Barack Obama, where the former US president was interviewed by the writer and broadcaster Afua Hirsch.

Continue reading...
title: Barack Obama pays tribute to Manchester cotton workers and cites them as an inspiration

author: Robyn Vinter North of England correspondent
description:
Yorkshire ambulance service says workers may have accessed or attempted to access information ‘without legitimate reason’

NHS staff may have accessed the medical records of a man killed by a tiger at a wildlife park “without legitimate permission”, an ambulance trust has said.

Yorkshire ambulance service NHS trust has launched an investigation into two members of staff at the trust, which responded to emergency calls on Saturday when William Chapman climbed into the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park.

Continue reading...
title: NHS staff investigated over potential accessing of tiger victim’s records

author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
description:
Abhijeet Dipke was arrested before planned anti-government demonstrations in Delhi

The leader of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) youth movement, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained by police on Friday as authorities cracked down on fresh anti-government protests in the Indian capital.

Dipke was detained before a planned Friday evening demonstration he had called in central Delhi, urging supporters of the movement to come out and hold up the Indian flag.

Continue reading...
title: India’s Cockroach Janta party leader detained amid crackdown on protests

author: Raphael Boyd
description:
A GOP loss in Texas would be a major blow for the US president and the Republicans

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Donald Trump has accused fellow Republicans of “doing everything possible to make it hard” for Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee in the Texas Senate race.

Katie Zacharia, the White House’s new press secretary, has stated that it is “unknown” how much she will engage with the press or hold briefings with reporters, as questions about her legal credentials continue to be asked following revelations that she failed to pass failed the California bar exam after graduating from law school.

Donald Trump has labeled a series of Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries as a “disgrace” while describing the the country’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy as “more difficult ​to deal with ​than Putin”.
title: Trump attacks fellow Republicans for ‘hurting Texas’ during senate election race – US politics live

author: Taz Ali
description:
The prime minister is expected to announce plans on devolving decision-making powers away from both Westminster and Holyrood towards regions and towns

John Healey is poised to tax Britain’s banks in his 28 October budget, to help offset the damage inflicted on the public finances by war in the Middle East, the Guardian understands.

The chancellor is in Bangkok, where the International Monetary Fund has praised the UK’s progress towards balancing the books, urging him to “stay the course”.

During my first week in office, I told the first minister that I wanted to work with him to spread opportunities to communities across Scotland’s regions and cities.

Through No10 North, we are rewiring the state and I want to make sure regions in Scotland are fully part of this.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham to deliver speech in Scotland on devolution – UK politics live

author: Oliver Holmes
description:
Images from New Zealand aerial survey of Nikumaroro in 1938 offer new clues over aviator’s disappearance

A New Zealand museum has released nearly 50 photos from a 1938 aerial survey of the island where Amelia Earhart is believed to have crash-landed, offering amateur sleuths new evidence to scour for traces of the pioneering aviator and her plane.

The black-and-white images were published by the Air Force Museum of New Zealand after renewed interest in one of the biggest mysteries of the 20th century, spurred by a US expedition to the Pacific atoll of Nikumaroro in search of new clues.

Continue reading...
title: Museum releases historical photos of island where Amelia Earhart may have crashed

author: Press Association
description:
Joshua Foster pleaded guilty over death of toddler who fell from fourth-floor window of hotel during family holiday

A British man has been handed a €3,000 (£2,500) fine after his two-year-old son fell nearly 12 metres (40ft) to his death from the fourth floor window of a hotel in Cyprus.

Joshua Foster thought the window was closed when he placed the boy on a sill to show him the view of a waterpark and “lost control” of him, the court previously heard.

Continue reading...
title: British man fined €3,000 for causing two-year-old son’s death in Cyprus

author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
description:
As violent spirits are unleashed in Sky’s Possession, observers see confident creatives reclaiming the island’s narratives in a form of ‘cultural reparation’

A woman opens a 300‑year‑old box, unleashing a violent spirit – it is the spirit of colonialism and oppression roaring back to life. It is a pivotal scene in Sky’s supernatural series Possession and symbolises a wider shift in Jamaica’s film industry, where directors are increasingly using the landscape to tell Jamaican stories – including those that confront enslavement, trauma and historical memory.

The series is about a biracial British lawyer who travels to Jamaica to investigate a multimillion-pound inheritance dispute, only to uncover a dark, vengeful spirit tied to the plantation’s brutal colonial past.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Opening the lid of a horrible secret’: Jamaicans confront enslavement with taboo-busting stories on screen

author: Matt Andrews and Ed Walton for MetDesk
description:
Landslide blocks river and triggers downstream flooding, while summer temperatures persist in Portugal

Flash floods have swept through Nepal’s central Gorkha district after a pre-dawn landslide on 11 October blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering severe downstream flooding. At least five people have died, and almost 100 have been rescued. Two villages in the worst-affected Chumanubri rural municipality were reportedly destroyed, with homes, roads and bridges washed away. Part of a hydropower station was also damaged.

After river levels surged from 2 metres to nearly 8.5 metres within hours, the national disaster risk reduction and management authority reported that 204 homes were damaged, and more than 650 people had been affected. More than 100 foreign trekkers were stranded in the popular hiking region. The floods come just two months after catastrophic flooding and landslides devastated p
title: Flash floods kill five and destroy villages in central Nepal

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
European leaders are meeting in Brussels amid worsening relations between Washington and Kyiv

Denmark’s prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, has also acknowledged the situation is very difficult given tensions with the US just as winter is “fast approaching.”

“We must continue to support Ukraine. Otherwise we are making things far too easy for the Russians,” she said.

Continue reading...
title: EU’s von der Leyen pledges to ‘not lift any sanctions unless Russia stops the war’ as leaders discuss Ukraine – Europe live

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Reform MP defends leader after ITV footage shows official warning Farage he is ‘protecting’ candidate over racist David Lammy comments

The Reform UK MP Robert Jenrick sought to defend the party against fresh allegations that it hosts extremists by claiming that Nigel Farage had “probably done more than almost anybody to stand against racism and the far right.”

The remarks came after Farage was berated by a Reform official for “protecting” a mayoral candidate who was accused of making racist remarks against the former Labour deputy prime minister, David Lammy.

Continue reading...
title: Jenrick claims Farage has done more to stand against racism than ‘almost anybody’

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
David Shoebridge says 47-page document not ‘made by, used by, or seen by’ his office as matter referred to parliamentary standards commission

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Greens leader David Shoebridge has denied knowledge of the existence of an alleged crisis management document on how to deal with allegations against Jordon Steele-John being made public.

The Nine newspapers reported on Friday afternoon the existence of a “secret dossier”, first drafted in 2016, which contained misconduct allegations against the Western Australian Greens senator and how to suppre
title: Greens leader denies knowledge of ‘secret dossier’ on how to handle Jordon Steele-John misconduct allegations

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Eight-year-old Queensland girl died in 2022 after being denied insulin by her religious parents

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Elizabeth Struhs’ child protection case was not “prioritised” or worked intensively because the staff member assigned to her case was “very busy”, a coroner has heard.

The Queensland coroner’s court also heard the case worker may have been “overly influenced” by the presentation of Struhs’ “upper class home”, putting cases believed to involve a more immediate risk ahead of Elizabeth’s.

Continue reading...
title: Elizabeth Struhs’ child protection case not ‘prioritised’ due to high workload, inquest hears

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Announcement comes a day after Liberal and Labor parties say they will cover out-of-pocket costs for abortion care

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation has proposed a $2,000 baby bonus for new parents in Victoria – a day after the Labor and Liberal parties both agreed to cover out-of-pocket costs for abortion care.

The deputy leader of One Nation in Victoria, Colleen Harkin, announced the plan on Friday to remove out-of-pocket costs for pregnant women in the public healthcare system and a $2,000 subsidy for those accessing private maternity care.

Continue reading...
title: One Nation proposes $2,000 baby subsidy in Victoria but says it won’t touch state abortion laws

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Bruce Hales also denies church was a cult while son tells parliamentary committee it was ‘a bit rough’ being labelled as such

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The most senior member of the Exclusive Brethren has denied any knowledge of or involvement in thousands of members from his church volunteering for the Liberal party at the 2025 election.

The Plymouth Brethren christian church has rejected claims it coordinated volunteers and a campaign for the Coalition, and that it secretly paid far-right figures to stage stunts against the prime minister and other Labor MPs.
title: Exclusive Brethren head denies knowing church members were volunteering for Liberal party during 2025 election

author: Nino Bucci
description:
Accused war criminal announces venture with video on Instagram of him walking along beach and working out

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Accused war criminal Ben Roberts-Smith has launched a brand, saying he needs the income to support his family and fund his legal expenses after being charged with murdering or ordering the murders of five unarmed detainees while deployed in Afghanistan between 2009 and 2012.

Roberts-Smith launched the label with a video on Instagram of him walking along a beach on the Gold Coast and working out, soundtracked by media reports about him being awarded the Victoria Cross and his subsequent arrest. The video included the caption: “Get ready….the time has come. #neveroutofthefight #under
title: ‘It’s about the underdog’: Ben Roberts-Smith launches brand to support family amid legal battle

author: Associated Press
description:
• 21-year-old was treated on field after injury during game

  • Coach pays tribute to player’s ‘quiet strength’

Southern Nazarene University in Oklahoma announced on Thursday that sophomore safety Tyler Ulrich has died five days after sustaining what the school called a “traumatic injury” during a game against Ouachita Baptist. Ulrich was 21.

The Division II school based in Bethany, Oklahoma, did not reveal the cause of death or the nature of Ulrich’s injury. Ulrich was hurt during a 49-14 loss on Saturday, with the game delayed for nearly an hour while he received medical attention before being transported to a hospital.

Continue reading...
title: College football player Tyler Ulrich dies five days after ‘traumatic injury’ during game

author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland, with Arwa Mahdawi, produced by Nada Smiljanic and Danielle Stephens and the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
description:
The US vice-president is following the Donald Trump playbook, attacking the Democrats, attempting to make jokes and even swearing more. Jonathan Freedland talks to Arwa Mahdawi about why Vance is making such an effort to court voters

Buy your tickets to the Guardian’s post-midterm live event, hosted by Jonathan Freedland

Watch Jonathan Freedland on our new Politics Weekly YouTube channel

Send your questions and feedback to politicsweeklyamerica@theguardian.com

Watch Today in Focus’ episode on the Trump administration investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar

Read David Smith’s piece on Katie Z
title: Is JD Vance campaigning for the midterms … or 2028? – podcast

author: Ben Doherty
description:
Widespread manhunt in city’s inner west after man reportedly seen carrying longarm weapon

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A large swathe of Dulwich Hill in Sydney’s inner west has been locked down by police as they search for a man reportedly carrying a shotgun.

The man allegedly set alight a stolen car and menaced witnesses with the weapon before fleeing on foot.

Continue reading...
title: Sydney suburb Dulwich Hill in lockdown as police search for man seen with shotgun

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Jeff Bacon, managing director of Oceania Precision, has been described by the NSW party’s leader as ‘my go-to man on the firearms industry’

A firearms manufacturer hoping to represent One Nation in New South Wales wants to repeal gun laws introduced following the Bondi beach massacre, after arguing “every single one” of the rifles he produces was banned in the state.

Earlier this month, One Nation’s NSW leader, Mike Newman, and the federal MP Barnaby Joyce revealed Jeff Bacon would be second on the party’s upper house ticket in the March state election.

Continue reading...
title: Firearms manufacturer standing for One Nation in NSW opposes post-Bondi gun laws that reclassify weapons

author: Gabrielle Canon
description:
The remains of Edward Lelburian Jackson were first discovered in 2022, and an initial autopsy revealed he was killed decades ago

After four years, a piece of the haunting mystery uncovered in the waning waters of drought-stricken Lake Mead has been solved.

Since the remains of an unknown homicide victim were discovered stuffed inside a barrel in 2022, Las Vegas investigators have been searching not for his killer – but for his identity. At a press conference on Thursday, Clark county coroner Melanie Rouse shared his name publicly for the first time: Edward Lelburian Jackson.

Continue reading...
title: Police reveal identity of man found in a barrel in drought-stricken Lake Mead
